rect.title: This diagram is drawn from ply.yaml, the file describing this codebase's architecture and verification claims. Each box is a component; chips are functions with their declared checks; arrows are permitted calls (solid) and data flows (dashed); red bars are forbidden calls. A box's grey depth is how strongly it promises to be checked — white means something inside promises nothing, deeper grey means stronger checks promised, and the weakest function sets the whole box's shade. Nothing here is green: green is kept for evidence a run has actually earned, which this render never sees, so a picture full of promises should not look like a picture full of results. Hover anything for its meaning.

g.title: ply.yaml — the document this picture is drawn from. Everything you see here was declared in it; nothing was inferred from code. What each box has actually been checked for is what `cargo ply verify` reports, not this drawing. ply: 1 — the format version every rule below is read under; a version this build does not speak is refused, never guessed at

What this document declares. "0 functions promise nothing" counts functions that end up with nothing checked -- whether nobody wrote any checks for them, or the document switched checking off for them on purpose. Running `cargo ply verify` is what turns promises into results; this line never reports results.

component e2e — maps to Rust module ply_e2e Drives the built binary the way a user does, and depends on nothing. A suite that links the library instead stops testing what ships. It had grown exactly that dependency once; the fix was to move the test rather than widen the rule. promises nothing as a whole — something inside declares no checks, and one unchecked thing sets the level of everything around it (unclaimed) hollow — declares nothing inside yet: no functions, no nested components. Nothing to zoom into; a sketch waiting for claims.

component attrs — maps to Rust module ply_attrs Stands alone. It is a proc-macro crate, compiled for the machine doing the building rather than the machine the program will run on, so a dependency from here into the library would compile perfectly well and would be wrong: the macro would begin depending on the very thing it exists to annotate. promises nothing as a whole — something inside declares no checks, and one unchecked thing sets the level of everything around it (unclaimed) hollow — declares nothing inside yet: no functions, no nested components. Nothing to zoom into; a sketch waiting for claims.

component core — maps to Rust module ply_core Everything Ply knows how to do, with no terminal attached. It must never reach up into the command-line layer: that constraint is what makes the engine adapters testable at all, because the moment a diagnostic's wording lives here, the wording and the engine can only be tested together. state Envelope — the structure this component holds, where `owns` says who may change one. The rows below are its fields: each name was found in the code, and each shape read off what that field really is promises nothing as a whole — something inside declares no checks, and one unchecked thing sets the level of everything around it (unclaimed)

command — one of the things this component holds; the block with a line written across it means text. Written in the code as `String`. The name came from the document; the shape and the type came from the code, so this row cannot say something the source does not.

root — one of the things this component holds; the two overlapping outlines mean a structure of your own -- there is more inside it than this row shows. Written in the code as `Node`. The name came from the document; the shape and the type came from the code, so this row cannot say something the source does not. The hatching means Ply has no way to make one of these, which is usually why the functions around it come back unchecked.

diagnostics — one of the things this component holds; the three stacked bars mean a list: many values, kept in the order they were put in. Written in the code as `Vec<Diagnostic>`. The name came from the document; the shape and the type came from the code, so this row cannot say something the source does not. The hatching means Ply has no way to make one of these, which is usually why the functions around it come back unchecked.

coverage — one of the things this component holds; the dashed outline means the value might not be there at all. Written in the code as `Option<Coverage>`. The name came from the document; the shape and the type came from the code, so this row cannot say something the source does not. The hatching means Ply has no way to make one of these, which is usually why the functions around it come back unchecked.

component kernel — maps to Rust module ply_core::kernel Decides what a pile of results adds up to: the order that ranks one kind of evidence above another, the rule that a parent is never reported as stronger than its weakest part, and the flags that travel upward beside a verdict without being confused for one. It is kept deliberately small and free of special cases, and its rules are checked by trying every shape of result tree up to a size. promises nothing as a whole — something inside declares no checks, and one unchecked thing sets the level of everything around it (unclaimed) hollow — declares nothing inside yet: no functions, no nested components. Nothing to zoom into; a sketch waiting for claims.

component engines — maps to Rust module ply_core::engines The adapters that drive each outside checking tool as a separate program and read back what it said. Ply never re-implements a checker; everything here is translation, in both directions. promises nothing as a whole — something inside declares no checks, and one unchecked thing sets the level of everything around it (unclaimed) hollow — declares nothing inside yet: no functions, no nested components. Nothing to zoom into; a sketch waiting for claims.

component harness — maps to Rust module ply_core::harness Works out what a function's inputs are and whether Ply can make one of each. This is the part that decides whether a function can be checked at all, and it is where a refusal gets its reason. promises nothing as a whole — something inside declares no checks, and one unchecked thing sets the level of everything around it (unclaimed) hollow — declares nothing inside yet: no functions, no nested components. Nothing to zoom into; a sketch waiting for claims.

component visual — maps to Rust module ply_core::visual The drawing, the prose form of the same facts, and the portable package an editor reads. Nothing here decides anything; it only shows what was decided. promises nothing as a whole — something inside declares no checks, and one unchecked thing sets the level of everything around it (unclaimed) hollow — declares nothing inside yet: no functions, no nested components. Nothing to zoom into; a sketch waiting for claims.

component record — maps to Rust module ply_core::record What was checked, and everything a result depended on. A stored result is only reused when every one of those inputs still hashes the same, which is what stops a stale green outliving the code that earned it. promises nothing as a whole — something inside declares no checks, and one unchecked thing sets the level of everything around it (unclaimed) hollow — declares nothing inside yet: no functions, no nested components. Nothing to zoom into; a sketch waiting for claims.

component report — maps to Rust module ply_cli::audit Says what this codebase's evidence rests on that Ply never checks -- the promises taken on trust, listed rather than assumed. promises nothing as a whole — something inside declares no checks, and one unchecked thing sets the level of everything around it (unclaimed) hollow — declares nothing inside yet: no functions, no nested components. component render — maps to Rust module ply_render Draws a document before any code exists, and writes the same facts as prose. It is the surface a reader judges the whole tool by, which is why its wording is tested by exact string rather than by shape. promises nothing as a whole — something inside declares no checks, and one unchecked thing sets the level of everything around it (unclaimed) hollow — declares nothing inside yet: no functions, no nested components. component check — maps to Rust module ply_check The standalone spec validator, which predates the installed `cargo ply check` command and overlaps it. Retiring one of the two is recorded work, not a decision taken here. promises nothing as a whole — something inside declares no checks, and one unchecked thing sets the level of everything around it (unclaimed) hollow — declares nothing inside yet: no functions, no nested components. cli -> core — cli may call core. That an undeclared cross-component call is forbidden is declared here, and not checked by this build: Ply currently compares crate-level dependencies and does not yet look inside functions, so a call that crosses this line can still go unnoticed (§5.3)

render -> core — render may call core. That an undeclared cross-component call is forbidden is declared here, and not checked by this build: Ply currently compares crate-level dependencies and does not yet look inside functions, so a call that crosses this line can still go unnoticed (§5.3)
